name: Paroxetine
summary: An SSRI with strong efficacy across anxiety disorders but a heavier side-effect load — sexual dysfunction, weight gain, and the most prominent discontinuation syndrome of the class.
mechanism: Selectively inhibits serotonin reuptake via SERT; also has mild anticholinergic and noradrenergic-reuptake effects.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic, CYP2D6 (substrate and inhibitor) with saturable (nonlinear) kinetics

dosing.adult: 20 mg once daily (morning); usual range 20–40 mg/day

safety.pregnancy: Historical (controversial) association with cardiac malformations; generally avoided in pregnancy when alternatives exist.
safety.lactation: Enters breast milk; limited data — monitor infant.
warnings: Black-box warning: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults (≤24 y) early in treatment
Serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs
Anticholinergic effects greater than other SSRIs
monitoring: Mood and suicidality early in treatment
Signs of serotonin syndrome or discontinuation symptoms
safety.overdose: Overdose is generally well tolerated; serotonin syndrome and seizures are possible.

clinicalPearls: Shortest half-life SSRI with anticholinergic properties — the hardest SSRI to discontinue; taper slowly.
Potent CYP2D6 inhibitor with nonlinear kinetics — dose-dependent side effects and interactions.
good: Anxiety-predominant depression or panic/social anxiety where a well-studied SSRI is needed.
bad: Patients prone to sexual dysfunction, weight gain, or missed doses (withdrawal), or with pregnancy concerns.
